newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX spot crude ends sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX spot crude ends sharply lower.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended sharply lower Friday after the spot month fell below $19.00 a barrel for the first time in over a year as ample supply continued to hammer oil prices.
"With a move like today you can't just buy indiscriminately. Another $1.00 move would not be beyond the situation," said Bob Yawger, of E.D. & F Man International Inc. in New York.
May crude ended off 35 cents at $19.12 a barrel. May gasoline closed off 0.42 cent at 60.48 cents a gallon. May heating oil ended off 0.12 cent at 53.14 cents a gallon.
Shortly before the close, the spot crude contract hit a session low of $18.96, the first time the spot slipped below $19.00 since March 4, 1994, when it reached $18.78.
Crude has been trading at its lowest point in more than a year this week as imports from West Africa and North Sea created a surfeit in the U.S. Gulf where refinery demand is concentrated.
Spot crude has lost $3.50 since mid-March with half the loss seen this week alone.
"There is a lot of supply in the Atlantic Basin, partly because OPEC continues to produce over their quotas," said a NYMEX player.
Selling accelerted after crude broke technical support of $19.35, which was created by this past Tuesday's session low and was the lowest point for spot crude since March 11, 1996.
But crude may find some technical support.

Pegasus Econometric Research noted channel support for Friday on crude's spot continuation chart at $18.80, created by a descending trendline that extends through the low March 3 of $19.96 and on the upper end, from the high January 31 of $25.00.
A touch of cold weather next week, may also help the crude market, although some traders said they think the colder temperatures may be shrugged off.

Gasoline and heating oil, meanwhile, were up most of the session before succumbing to crude's downfall. Both products had found early strength in news that a fire at Tosco Corp's Wilmington, California, refinery shut a unit which makes gasoline and jet fuel.
Tosco said it did not know when the 25,000 barrel-per-day unit would restart.
